hiring.body_html:
You roast on a 12 kg Probat, four batches a morning, for the two cafés and about 40 wholesale accounts.

  • Start 06:30. Roasting is done by 11:00, then cupping and packing.
  • Two Saturdays a month, with the following Tuesday off.
  • Green coffee arrives on Wednesdays — everyone helps unload.

We will teach you the profile software. What you do need is to be comfortable working alone in the early hours.

roasterCare.live_meta: 12 kg drum · Kiyosumi roasting room · roasting held since 06:12
roasterCare.live_spoken: “Exhaust won’t come back down after the second batch. Damper’s still on 4, and I can smell the chaff from here.”
roasterCare.live_answer:
It only starts on the second batch, and that is the useful part — the drum is already hot by then, so the exhaust side is worth looking at before the burner.

Three things fit that shape:

- Chaff collector — last serviced 29 July, 212 batches ago. R-2 is on a 150-batch interval.
- Fan belt — retensioned 2 August after the same complaint. The log records the work but not who signed it off.
- Damper linkage sitting a notch off 4.

Reading the last 40 minutes off the controller now — the chaff sensor has been
roasterCare.proc_meta: Assembled from the last six services on R-2 and the manufacturer sheet (rev 4).
roasterCare.proc_body:
Do this cold. The collector body stays above 60 °C for roughly 25 minutes after the last drop, and the gasket deforms if you unseat it hot.

## Steps

1. Cut power at the panel, not at the controller — the controller keeps the fan spinning down for another 90 seconds.
2. Release the two draw latches on the cyclone. The third latch on R-2 was replaced with a bolt in May, so you need a 13 mm spanner as well.
3. Lift the canister straight out. It weighs about 9 kg full and the lip catches on the frame if you tilt it.

- [x] Panel locked out
- [x] Canister emptied and weighed
- [ ] Cyclone wall wiped down
- [ ] Gasket checked for glazing
- [ ] Latch torque re-checked

| Fastener | Torque | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cyclone latch | 12 N·m | Both sides, alternating |
| Bolt (R-2, third latch) | 18 N·m | 13 mm, fitted 2026-05-14 |
| Fan housing | 9 N·m | Do not seat hard against the gasket |

> If the gasket has gone shiny rather than matte, replace it. A glazed gasket passes a visual check and still leaks about 4% of the airflow.

Reset the batch counter with `roastctl service --reset chaff` once the canister is back on, or the next interval will be counted from the wrong place.
roasterCare.record_body:
### Signatures

| Date | Batches | Fitter | Signed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-07-29 | 148 | Ines Bardem | Yes |
| 2026-06-11 | 163 | Kwabena Osei | Yes |
| 2026-05-14 | 151 | Ines Bardem | Yes |
| 2026-04-02 | 139 | Hana Morikawa | — |
| 2026-02-19 | 155 | Kwabena Osei | Yes |
| 2026-01-08 | 144 | Ines Bardem | Yes |

The April entry has no signature. The canister was serviced — the emptied weight is in the log — but the sheet went back in the folder unsigned, so the interval clock never reset.

That is why the counter now reads 212 against an interval of 150. The machine has not skipped a service; the paperwork skipped one.

roasterCare.profile_note: Same beans as last week, but servicing the collector puts the airflow back to nominal, and the old damper step now overshoots. This keeps the drop temperature and gives back the 35 seconds that development had been losing.
